items.text: Who gets your first "thank you" today?
What you see today passes through a memory filter. One word, this morning.
Offer a word to today's filter before you head out.
Feel the morning air, and say "thank you," once.
Who is the person you most want to see today?
If you named the feeling you woke up with, what would it be?
Before today's plans, take a moment to settle inside.
What matters most to you today?
To this new day: "thank you," once.
What if what you see today looked a little different?
To your first step today: "I love you," once.
What kind of self do you want to be today?
Give your current feeling one ×.
Let the afternoon begin from how you feel right now, too.
Offer a word to what you just heard, before moving on.
To the morning so far: "thank you," once.
Try letting your shoulders soften, just a little, right now.
A word to the afternoon's filter.
To the tiredness right now: "thank you," once.
To today, so far: "I love you," once.
Whatever you see or hear this afternoon, one word to the filter.
If you named your mood right now, what would it be?
To this midday breath: "thank you," once.
The afternoon, too, can be released with one word.
This is enough for today. Release it with one word, and sleep.
Before sleep, one "thank you" to everything you saw and heard today.
Today's portion can be released now.
Once in bed, leave today's filter outside.
To the heaviest feeling of today: "I love you," once.
Leave the rest to tomorrow's you. Good night.
Offer one word to today, and close your eyes.
Tonight, releasing and sleeping is enough.
To the quiet before sleep: "thank you," once.
Set down today's events, one by one.
Who will tonight's one word be for?
Before the light goes out, "thank you" to today.
(small bell) Right now. Right here.
(bell) Which filter are you looking through right now? One "thank you."
(bell) One word, for this very moment.
(bell) What's replaying, right now?
(bell) "Thank you" to the sound you hear right now.
(bell) "I love you" to yourself, right now.
(bell) Pause here, just a little.
(bell) Are your shoulders tense, right now?
(bell) Offer a word to the view in front of you, right now.
(bell) What were you just thinking, right now?
(bell) "Thank you" to this one breath.
(bell) Come back to right here, right now.
(bell) One word, for how you feel right now.
(bell) Right now, you don't need to know anything.
